item.title: Least Expensive Standard Pensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.15211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The paper proposes generating annuity payment streams at far lower costs than those implied by traditional theories. For a given investment universe, this enables the design of a least expensive standard pension, providing accurate monthly payments of savings account units over a set period. Such a standard pension invests dynamically in the savings account and the equity market's growth-optimal portfolio to replicate riskless payments with high accuracy at the lowest possible cost. Since this mathematically grounded standard pension is reliable and, by orders of magnitude, less expensive than traditional pensions, it provides a unique opportunity to improve the health of pension systems and provide more benefits for retirees.
item.dc:creator: Eckhard Platen

item.title: Dynamic Scenario-Based Portfolio Optimization for Multi-Asset ETFs
item.description: arXiv:2611.16540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Portfolio outcomes may depend as much on trading restrictions as on how returns are modeled. We compared historical moving-window returns with conditional scenarios from ARMA--GARCH models and a Student-$t$ copula for 30 U.S.-listed exchange-traded funds. Matched mean--variance and conditional value-at-risk portfolios were evaluated under long-only and limited long--short bounds over 946 sessions. Historical portfolios had higher observed reward--risk ratios in most comparisons, but no paired difference remained significant after multiple-testing adjustment. Conditional scenarios did not consistently reduce realized downside risk. We distinguished changes in target weights from trades required to rebalance holdings after market movements. Relaxing the target-adjustment limit changed exposures, turnover, and some returns more than varying scenario count or seed in the examined tests. These findings suggest that assessments of conditional return inputs should consider portfolio constraints and trading requirements.
item.dc:creator: Abigail A. Mensah, Ali M. Jaffri, Nicholas Appiah W. Brent Lindquist, Svetlozar T. Rachev, Frank J. Fabozzi

item.title: Conformal Risk Certificates for Portfolio Optimization Under Uncertainty: A Gated Reinforcement-Learning Approach
item.description: arXiv:2611.14699v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement-learning portfolio policies can optimize allocations from prices, covariances, and prior positions, yet they lack a calibrated, replayable mechanism for certifying that a proposed allocation respects a bounded risk envelope before execution. Regulators increasingly expect automated portfolio systems to provide exactly this kind of pre-trade audit trail, interpretable risk limit, and human-oversight mechanism. Gated Conformal Semantic Risk Control addresses this gap by separating return-seeking allocation from text-conditioned downside-risk verification. An instruction-tuned language model maps timestamped disclosures into schema-validated semantic risk states over macro, liquidity, earnings, and sector channels. These states induce correlated ellipsoidal factor-shock uncertainty sets whose conformal radii are calibrated by rolling finite-sample prediction over localized semantic nonconformity buckets. An asymmetric second-order cone gate then checks each raw PPO proposal against a certified worst-case semantic loss budget. The gate stays inactive for compliant proposals and intervenes only when that budget is exceeded. In walk-forward out-of-sample tests on nine liquid U.S. Select Sector SPDR ETFs, Raw PPO earns a 12.7% annual return while incurring a 4.05% semantic violation rate. Gated-CSRC removes all observed out-of-sample semantic limit breaches while retaining an 11.7% annual return. This 100-basis-point auditable safety premium is smaller than the yield loss imposed by unconditional hard projection, and exact McNemar testing confirms the compliance gain at $p < 10^{-15}$. Loughran-McDonald lexicon controls and time-shuffled text controls fail to reproduce this certificate.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Zarei, Amirhossein MohammadpourAzari, Moslem Habibi

item.title: Diffusion models for dynamic volatility surface generation and data-driven hedging
item.description: arXiv:2609.13402v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a diffusion-model framework for dynamic implied-volatility surface generation and evaluate its economic usefulness through data-driven hedging. The framework consists of two models. AD-Seq-Vol jointly learns the conditional evolution of the underlying asset return and the high-dimensional implied-volatility surface, generating adapted multi-period scenarios by sequentially updating the realized market history. AD-Seq-Vol-FT further incorporates option-market structure through post-training penalties for violations of static no-arbitrage conditions. Using daily SPX option data from 2000 to 2023, we show that the proposed models generate coherent surface trajectories while capturing both cross-sectional and temporal dependence. AD-Seq-Vol produces fewer and less severe static-arbitrage violations than the training data and the GAN-based benchmark, while AD-Seq-Vol-FT reduces these violations to nearly zero. We then integrate the generated conditional scenarios into an optimization-based hedging framework. Compared to a range of classical and data-driven benchmarks, the diffusion-based hedges maintain tracking errors near zero, substantially reduce tail risk, and exhibit particularly stable performance during the COVID-19 market disruption. These results establish Adaptive Sequential Diffusion Models as a promising class of market-consistent and economically useful financial scenario generators. Our code is available at: https://github.com/yinbinhan/volatility-surface-simulation.
item.dc:creator: Yinbin Han, Jack Yuxiang Zhang, Manuel Torres, Fernando Acero, Renyuan Xu
